title: One curve type: CurveGeometry with per-curve access, a closed flag and attributes, over the polyline helpers
user-messages:

description:
Split out of MESH-92 on 2026-11-05. The node graph's curve type, `CurveGeometry` (geometry/mesh/data/bundle), and the polyline helpers `PolylineResample` and `PolylineSimplify` (geometry/grid2d) are two ways to hold one thing: a sequence of points. Make `CurveGeometry` the one curve type and keep the array helpers as the maths underneath it.

What is duplicated today:
- Eight node files split a `CurveGeometry` into curves by hand from `curveOffsets()`: BiRailLoftNode, BirailLoftMeshNode, CurveDeformNode, CurveSweepMeshNode, CurveToMeshNode, JoinCurvesNode, ResampleCurveNode, TransformGeometryNode.
- Nothing records whether a curve is closed, so consumers guess (BirailLoftMeshNode.isClosed compares endpoints).
- The loft nodes slice the packed arrays to call PolylineResample.

The change:
1. Move PolylineResample and PolylineSimplify out of geometry/grid2d (they are dimension-general) into a polyline or curve package; see IX-23 for where geometry packages are going.
2. Per-curve accessors on CurveGeometry (first point, point count of curve k); the eight nodes use them instead of offset arithmetic.
3. A closed flag per curve, set by the primitive nodes (circle closed, bezier open) and read by consumers instead of guessing.
4. Optional per-curve and per-point float attributes, which MESH-20's radius and tilt nodes and the picture-tracing nodes (the follow-up ticket) need, e.g. ShadingEdges' lit side, width and contrast.
5. `resampled(...)` and `simplified(...)` on CurveGeometry that run the helpers per curve; the loft nodes stop slicing.

ResampleCurveNode is not a duplicate of PolylineResample.uniform: it keeps every vertex and splits each segment into ceil(length/segLen) pieces, while uniform spaces a fixed count evenly by arc length. Keep both behaviours.

The 2D picture-outline callers of the helpers (TraceReference, TraceOutlines, PixelImage, SubjectOutline, ShadingEdges) stay on the array helpers in this ticket; the follow-up ticket moves them onto curves.
definition-of-done:
1. PolylineResample and PolylineSimplify live outside geometry/grid2d, and grid2d's package-info no longer describes them.
2. No node outside CurveGeometry computes a curve's start or count from curveOffsets() by hand.
3. CurveGeometry records closed per curve; the primitive nodes set it, and BirailLoftMeshNode and BiRailLoftNode read it instead of comparing endpoints.
4. CurveGeometry carries optional per-curve and per-point float attributes, preserved by JoinCurvesNode, ResampleCurveNode and TransformGeometryNode.
5. Every curve-using DSL under dsl/ gives bit-identical output to master, except where a curve's closedness was guessed differently before; each such change is recorded on the ticket with before/after.
6. Full suite passes; a launch entry and screenshot of a curve DSL (e.g. birail_loft_ribbon) under tmp/.
testing-plan:
1. Before the change, dump every curve DSL's final mesh and curve outputs (ResultChangingReuseBenchmark#graphMeshes in MESH-92 is the pattern) and compare after.
2. Unit tests for CurveGeometry's per-curve accessors, closed flag and attribute carry-through join/resample/transform.
3. Full mvn test.
unknowns: Should the closed flag default to the old endpoint guess for curves loaded from DSL literals, so existing DSLs do not change?
changes-made: PolylineResample and PolylineSimplify moved from geometry/grid2d to the new geometry/curve package (with package-info); grid2d's package-info no longer describes them. PolylineResample gains uniformPlacements (where each even sample falls: segment and fraction) and interpolated (values carried on the points read at those placements), so attributes follow positions; uniform is those two, bit-identical on every curve graph.

CurveGeometry is the one curve type: public final positions, curveOffsets, closed (per curve), pointAttributes and curveAttributes (named float arrays); per-curve firstPoint, pointCount(k), curvePositions(k); withPositions (transform/deform keep flags and attributes); resampled(n) (even arc length per curve, PolylineResample underneath), subdivided(spacing) (ResampleCurveNode's split rule, every input point kept, moved out of the node) and simplified(tolerance) (Douglas-Peucker per curve; a closed curve as its loop). simplified has no main caller yet; MESH-94 is meant to use it.

Closed representation: a closed curve stores each point once and sets its flag; the repeated-first-point convention is gone from CurveGeometry (TracedSurfacePath.drawnPolyline keeps it for the GL overlays). circle_curve sets closed, curve_bezier open, mesh_to_curve BOUNDARY closed when the walk returns to its start, spline_ring / spline_cut / loop_through_points and RingCandidates.curves from the path's own closed flag (new TracedSurfacePath.curve). curve_to_mesh, curve_sweep, birail_loft and bi_rail_loft read the flag; the three endpoint-distance guesses and their epsilon constants are deleted. Unknown answered: no DSL builds curves from literals; every producer knows closedness, so nothing falls back to a guess.

No node computes a curve's start or count from curveOffsets by hand: the eight nodes (BiRailLoft, BirailLoftMesh, CurveDeform, CurveSweepMesh, CurveToMesh, JoinCurves, ResampleCurve, TransformGeometry) use the accessors or withPositions/resampled/subdivided. Attributes carry through join_curves (union by name, 0 where a side lacks one; curve attributes from A, else B), resample_curve (interpolated) and transform_geometry/curve_deform (kept).

bi_rail_loft over closed rails now resamples them closed and wraps the last station to the first (it used to resample a closed rail open over its repeated point, giving a doubled, unwelded seam station); mismatched rails (one closed, one open) give empty geometry, as birail_loft already did. Its boundary_a, boundary_b and iso_curve outputs carry the rails' closedness instead of always being forced closed.

Measured with test/benchmark/CurveGraphsBenchmark (new): every geometry output of every node in birail_loft_ribbon, curve_sweep_tube, neck_armor, tool_quilt, varying_tube_test, torus_loop_through_points and fertility_rings, meshes plus curves drawn with a closed curve's start repeated, diff -r before/after. All graphs bit-identical except neck_armor downstream of bi_rail_loft (the closedness change): collar_surface faces 12430 -> 12432 (vertices 12432 both; seam welded), rivets per row 149 -> 148 (duplicate seam rivet gone), pipes same counts with no degenerate seam ring, final collar_trimmed 13814/19296 -> 13915/19411 verts/faces. The seam sits at +x, which neck_armor trims away, so the final render barely shows it.

Tests: unit/mesh/CurveGeometryTest (9: accessors, primitives' closed flag, resampled/subdivided/simplified with attributes, join/resample/transform carry, birail_loft wrap and mixed-rail refusal). Full mvn test 804/0 before the sync onto CRAW-77. Launch entry 'MESH-93: mesh-viewer' (neck_armor.dsl), screenshot tmp/mesh-93-neck-armor.png.

Consolidated (supersedes the first entry's helper move): PolylineResample and PolylineSimplify are deleted, and so is the geometry/curve package; their maths (even arc-length placement, the shared point interpolation, Douglas-Peucker) is inside CurveGeometry.resampled / subdivided / simplified, so no raw packed-array polyline API is left. Picture outlines are CurveGeometry in the z = 0 plane: CurveGeometry.planar(xy, closed), planarLoop(drawn xy) and drawnPlanar(curve). The repeated-first-point form exists only as CurveGeometry.drawnPositions / drawnPlanar, the output for GL line strips and SVG; TracedSurfacePath.drawnPolyline is removed (RingTool and RingAnchorOrderBenchmark use curve(...).drawnPositions(0)).

Callers moved onto CurveGeometry: TraceOutlines, TraceReference (outline and edges), PixelImage.outlines, SubjectOutline, ShadingEdges (simplified), MeshSkeletonComparator (resampled) and MeshSkeletonExtractor (simplified, with each joint's distance-field radius carried as a 'radius' point attribute instead of a kept-point mask). The stored outline and edge fields (SubjectOutline.outline, ShadingEdges.lines) stay float[] xy; MESH-94's tracing nodes make them curves.

TracedSurfacePath keeps its double-precision positions: about 50 reads feed the geodesic, crossing and ring-region maths, and float positions would move segmentation results. curve(...) is now its only way out to the curve type.

Verified bit-identical: CurveGraphsBenchmark dump identical to the previous run (diff -r); a scratch check against master's PolylineSimplify/PolylineResample sources gave 0 mismatches in 9320 comparisons (132 traced picture loops at 5 tolerances on both the loop and PixelImage paths, 2000 random open 2D lines, 3D skeleton simplify, open and closed resample). CurveGeometryTest gains the picture-loop round trip (10 tests).
review-summary: CurveGeometry is now the only curve type: the array polyline helpers are gone and their maths lives in it, so picture outlines, skeleton paths and graph curves all resample and simplify as curves. Radius, tilt and picture-tracing nodes need one type with closed flags and attributes.
